name: Baal-hanan
overview: Baal-hanan was a male Edomite who served as king of Edom, succeeding Shaul according to Genesis 36:38. His role as a monarch in the lineage of Edomite rulers highlights his importance in the history of this tribe. There are no additional notes provided about his reign or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Baal-hanan means 'Baal is gracious,' reflecting a theophoric element common in ancient Semitic names. This proper name, as recorded in Genesis 36:38, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries the cultural significance of invoking Baal in its meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Baal-hanan was the father of Achbor, establishing a direct familial relationship noted in Genesis 36:38. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Baal-hanan's significance lies in his position as a king of Edom, marking the continuation of Edomite leadership after Shaul. His mention in Genesis 36:38 situates him within the genealogical and historical framework that traces the rulers of Edom, providing insight into the lineage and governance of this neighboring nation to Israel.
